table2.note: International reporting portfolio, Renewable records, fixed FY2013 World Bank income classes. Archive fiscal years are retained; pooled endpoints are 2013–2015 and 2020–2022. table3.caption: Table 3. Record and package influence: source-informed contract exclusion
table3.note: International reporting portfolio, Renewable records, fixed FY2013 World Bank income classes. Archive fiscal years are retained; pooled endpoints are 2013–2015 and 2020–2022. Amounts are recorded nominal USD on heterogeneous archive/source financial bases. Missing amounts are excluded, not replaced by zero. Baseline is source-informed contract exclusion. Effects are deletion minus baseline share changes, with denominators and provider support recomputed in the already-approved influence outputs. Standard Bank has zero classified-share influence here because its regional amount is retained in observed totals but unallocated by income. The approximately USD1.72bn Guinea package is corroborated and includes Souapiti development and Kaleta restructuring; its influence does not establish an error or justify deletion. Source-treatment effects are reported separately in the SI and are not causal effects.

figure1.caption: Figure 1. Annual four-class allocation under the archive reference and two source-informed specifications. International reporting portfolio, Renewable records, fixed FY2013 World Bank income classes. Archive fiscal years are retained; pooled endpoints are 2013–2015 and 2020–2022. Amounts are recorded nominal USD on heterogeneous archive/source financial bases. Missing amounts are excluded, not replaced by zero. Lines show each class’s share of observed amounts with known recipient income for every year from 2013 through 2022; they are not smoothed trends. Source-informed contract exclusion removes the two Dogger export-contract entries; whole-block exclusion additionally removes the unresolved Dogger financing entry. Both apply the same amount, overlap and recipient-geography reconciliations. Standard Bank remains in observed international totals under its documented regional role but outside the classified denominator. Annual amounts, observed/classified denominators, unknown-income amounts and missingness counts accompany every plotted point in figure1_annual_data.csv.

figure2.caption: Figure 2. Pooled endpoint share changes and nominal amounts by income class. International reporting portfolio, Renewable records, fixed FY2013 World Bank income classes. Archive fiscal years are retained; pooled endpoints are 2013–2015 and 2020–2022. Amounts are recorded nominal USD on heterogeneous archive/source financial bases. Missing amounts are excluded, not replaced by zero. Panel a shows late-minus-early classified-share changes in percentage points. Panel b joins early (open) and late (filled) pooled nominal amounts; endpoints are sums across three years, not annual averages. Under both source-informed specifications, low-income amounts fall from USD3.013bn to USD2.785bn although their shares rise. Classified denominators (early/late, USD bn) are 23.455/18.156 for the archive, 19.520/14.100 for contract exclusion and 19.520/13.577 for whole-block exclusion. Source-informed early observed totals additionally include USD0.2375bn unallocated regional support; the late unknown-income amount is zero. Full coverage is retained in accompanying CSVs.

figure3.caption: Figure 3. High-income share-change accounting and Standard Bank regional-completion outer envelopes. International reporting portfolio, Renewable records, fixed FY2013 World Bank income classes. Archive fiscal years are retained; pooled endpoints are 2013–2015 and 2020–2022. Amounts are recorded nominal USD on heterogeneous archive/source financial bases. Missing amounts are excluded, not replaced by zero. Points show the classified-income accounting: provider-country composition, within-provider allocation, entry and exit sum to total change. Horizontal segments for the source-informed cases are exact case-specific regional-completion outer envelopes, not confidence intervals. Completion assigns only Standard Bank’s observed regional amount across the four-class simplex; it changes the denominator relative to the uncompleted classified-share point. It imposes no actual-country eligibility restrictions and is not a bound on total or true finance exposure. Componentwise extrema need not occur together. The enlarged within-provider panel retains the positive contract-exclusion versus negative whole-block contrast throughout the respective outer envelopes. Regional completion is restricted to the original population; the arithmetic-flag-exclusion family is separate.
